question: Should ClickClack core accept Cloudflare Access assertions as an account-provisioning authority for every valid identity in the configured Access audience, rather than keeping this trust model outside the core authentication surface?
rationale: The code can verify signatures and claims, but it cannot determine whether the repository should own this Cloudflare-specific authorization boundary or what deployment-policy guarantees are required for safe automatic user creation.

options.title: Approve with deployment proof
options.body: Accept the core integration after confirming the intended Access policy and obtaining redacted runtime proof of successful login, session reuse, and rejected invalid assertions.

options.title: Keep the existing auth model
options.body: Do not add this automatic-provisioning path to core and retain magic-link and OAuth login flows for Access-fronted deployments.

recommendation.title: Approve with deployment proof
recommendation.body: Accept the core integration after confirming the intended Access policy and obtaining redacted runtime proof of successful login, session reuse, and rejected invalid assertions.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor supplied the proposed authentication design and is the only concrete person connected to the affected path in the available history.
